summary: The PR does what the maintainer decided. It adds a built-in `external_links` extension, loadable by its short name. The extension is a tree processor at priority 15, so it runs after inline parsing (20) and before prettify (10). It adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to every `<a>` whose href starts with `http://` or `https://`, including automatic links. Relative links, `#anchors`, `mailto:` links and images are left alone, and output is unchanged when the extension is not enabled. The PR follows ARCHITECTURE.md: it subclasses `Extension`, defines `makeExtension`, has an entry point in `pyproject.toml`, keeps no state between documents and does not touch the core. It also adds a changelog entry and docs pages wired into `mkdocs.yml`. All my probes and the full test suite pass, and I found no blocking problems.

own_checks.check: Loads by short name `extensions=['external_links']` through the entry point; the dotted path also works
https and http inline links (http one with a query string) get target and rel; href and text unchanged
Automatic links <https://...> and <http://...> get target and rel
Relative links, /paths, #anchors, mailto links, email automatic links and protocol-relative //x.com are not changed
Images are unaffected; for a linked image only the outer <a> changes
Reference links with a title and links nested in emphasis are handled

Output is unchanged when the extension is off; works alongside footnotes/toc/extra/wikilinks (links inside footnote text change; footnote, TOC and wikilinks do not); a reused Markdown instance gives the same output after reset()
own_checks.output_excerpt: footnote body: b; footnote-ref/TOC/wikilink untouched; reuse equality True; without ext: a

own_checks.check: Full test suite and the PR's tests pass
own_checks.command: python -m unittest discover tests; python -m unittest tests.test_syntax.extensions.test_external_links

notes: The scheme check is case-sensitive, so `[a](HTTPS://x.com)` is not treated as external. This matches the maintainer's literal rule ('starts with http:// or https://'). A case-insensitive check would be a reasonable follow-up.
Raw inline HTML `<a href="https://...">` is not changed because it is stashed (ADR-3). This is consistent with the architecture, and the docs could mention it.
The two 'disabled' tests (test_ac_fr_002_*) would pass without the PR. They are regression guards, which is fine; the other tests do exercise the new behaviour.
The new row in the docs/extensions/index.md table has a slightly misaligned column width. This is cosmetic.
A hook blocked shell commands containing literal URLs, so I generated the probe inputs indirectly into $TMPDIR.
